name: Arianism
summary: The Son is a created being, the first and greatest of creatures; there was a time when the Son was not.

name: Semi-Arian or homoiousian subordinationism
summary: The Son is like the Father in being, or divine in a lesser, derived degree, but not of one substance with him.

name: Modalism (Sabellianism)
summary: Father, Son and Spirit are only modes, masks or roles of one divine person, not truly distinct.

name: Adoptionism
summary: Jesus was a mere man who was adopted as God's Son, at his baptism or resurrection.
condemned: Rejected in the 3rd century (Paul of Samosata, Antioch 268); excluded by 'begotten before all ages'

name: Psilanthropism (Ebionite and modern 'merely human' views)
summary: Jesus was only a human teacher or prophet and not God.
condemned: Excluded by 'true God from true God'

name: Pneumatomachianism (Macedonianism)
summary: The Holy Spirit is a created power or an impersonal force, not the Lord, and is not to be worshipped with the Father and the Son.
condemned: Constantinople (381), canon 1; the reason the third article was expanded

name: Docetism
summary: Christ only seemed to be human, or did not truly suffer and die.
condemned: Opposed in the New Testament (1 John 4:2) and by Ignatius of Antioch; excluded by 'was made man ... suffered and was buried'

name: Apollinarianism
summary: Christ had no human mind or rational soul; the divine Word took its place.

name: Gnostic dualism and Marcionism
summary: The material world was made by a lesser or evil god (a demiurge), not by the one true God; the God of the Old Testament is not the Father of Jesus.
condemned: Rejected in the 2nd century (Irenaeus, Against Heresies); excluded by 'Maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible'

name: Tritheism and polytheism
summary: Father, Son and Spirit are three separate gods, or there are many gods.

name: Marcellianism
summary: Christ's kingdom will come to an end, with the Son returning into the Father.
condemned: Constantinople (381), canon 1 (Marcellians); the clause 'whose kingdom shall have no end' was added against it

name: Denial of the virgin birth
summary: Jesus was conceived in the ordinary way with a human father.
condemned: Excluded by 'incarnate by the Holy Spirit of the Virgin Mary'

name: Denial of the bodily resurrection of Christ
summary: Jesus did not rise bodily; the resurrection is only a metaphor, a vision or the disciples' faith; or he did not truly die (swoon theory).
condemned: Excluded by 'rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures' (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:3-4, 14)

name: Denial of the return and judgement
summary: Christ will not come again, and there will be no judgement of the living and the dead.
condemned: Excluded by 'he shall come again, with glory, to judge'

name: Denial of the resurrection of the dead
summary: There is no resurrection of the dead and no life of the world to come; death is the end.
condemned: Excluded by 'we look for the resurrection of the dead' (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:12-19)

name: Denial of the Son's role in creation
summary: The Son had no part in creation; the world was made before or without him.
condemned: Excluded by 'by whom all things were made'
